leading_positions.synthesis: Four members explicitly prefer Mircea Cărtărescu (B012) as a single-writer configuration in round 1. They share a case built on a recognizable voice and formal control over very large structures in which memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation form one architecture, with Blinding and Solenoid as the main reference works. They also share the same reservations: their judgment rests on translation and reception, the Romanian syntax and rhythm cannot be assessed directly, and it is unresolved whether recurring motifs across the large novels amount to development or to elaboration of one mode. They share a drafting preference to anchor the citation in the prose project and treat the poetry as origin or background. They differ in the wording of that origin (mattson-ellen: 'grown from Romanian poetry'; palm-anna-karin: 'rooted in poetry'; sem-sandberg-steve: 'rooted in Romanian language and imagination'; olsson-anders: no poetry credit). They also differ in how firmly each judges that the later volumes deepen rather than repeat. Each also names a different first alternative: B043 (mattson-ellen), B002 (olsson-anders, palm-anna-karin, sem-sandberg-steve).

Two members explicitly prefer Adonis (B002) as a single-writer configuration in round 1. Their shared claim is that he remade Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and sustained dialogue with inherited forms, with Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses as representative works. They also share the view that timing and age are not literary criteria and that the essays should be a companion strand and not the basis of the award. Both name Cărtărescu (B012) as an alternative and B013 (Yoko Tawada) as the other alternative. Both concede that the central claim rests on Arabic prosody and intertextual play that the committee can assess only through translation, so the case rests more on reception and description than the prose case does. They differ in emphasis: carlberg-ingrid expresses open willingness to be persuaded by the Cărtărescu case, while sward-anne holds that translation risk bears harder on poetry than on prose and does not treat it as symmetrical. Four other members name Adonis as an alternative or high-ranked option (olsson-anders, palm-anna-karin, sem-sandberg-steve, mattson-ellen), but their round 1 statements do not make him their preferred configuration.

areas_of_agreement: All six round 1 files prefer a single-writer configuration with exactly one prize part, and all six treat Cărtărescu (B012) and Adonis (B002) as the two most serious candidates, either as a first preference or as a named alternative.

All six state that they have not independently verified sources, that translation limits direct assessment of the leading candidates, and that their judgments rest on public knowledge, reception and shortlist descriptions.

Members agree that age, timing, fame and political positioning are not literary merit, and that a citation for Adonis should be centred on the poetry with the essays as a secondary or companion strand.
Members who discuss Cărtărescu agree that a citation for him should name the prose project and should not claim more for the poetry and shorter prose than the evidence supports.

Members across both camps identify the same open test for Cărtărescu: whether recurrence of imagery in the large novels is development or elaboration of a single mode, and whether scale is being mistaken for finished execution.

Members accept that narrow or compact corpora (Michon) and hybrid forms (Magris, Carson) are legitimate literary achievements but raise open questions about breadth of significance across the whole oeuvre.
scientific_disputes: Which achievement carries more literary weight under the common criteria: renewing the poetic language of a whole literary tradition over decades (Adonis, as argued by carlberg-ingrid and sward-anne) or constructing a sustained, formally controlled prose cosmos at very large scale (Cărtărescu, as argued by the four B012 supporters).

Whether translation risk is roughly symmetrical between the two lead candidates (the view expressed by olsson-anders, palm-anna-karin and sem-sandberg-steve) or bears harder on poetry because the claim lies in prosody and sound (the view expressed by sward-anne).

Whether the Cărtărescu case is more directly testable from available translations (carlberg-ingrid concedes this) or whether long, intricate sentences may be inflated or flattened in translation (palm-anna-karin, sem-sandberg-steve, olsson-anders).
Whether concentration of a compact corpus is a form of depth (mattson-ellen on Michon) or a limit on significance across a body of work (olsson-anders, palm-anna-karin, sem-sandberg-steve).

Whether the fiction within Magris's hybrid travel, essay and fiction oeuvre meets the criteria of linguistic and imaginative invention as sharply as higher-ranked candidates; olsson-anders asks for a fuller case and no member has yet supplied one.
attribution_disputes: No member disputes that each entry names exactly one writer. The two leading configurations differ in laureate (Cărtărescu versus Adonis), not in the number of names or the structure of the prize.

The proposed Adonis citations from carlberg-ingrid and sward-anne are worded as for 'a poetic and critical oeuvre', yet both members say the citation should be anchored in the poetry with the essays secondary. It is unresolved whether the wording should be narrowed to the poetry alone.

The four proposed Cărtărescu citations differ in how they treat the poetry: as origin or root (mattson-ellen, palm-anna-karin), as Romanian language and imagination (sem-sandberg-steve), or not at all (olsson-anders). Whether the citation should name the poetry, and how, is not settled.

Several members note that their coverage of Cărtărescu's poetry and early prose, and of Adonis's later collections and essays, is thinner than of the best-known works. This bears on how much a citation can claim.
maturity_disputes: For Cărtărescu: whether the late large-scale work extends the method of the earlier trilogy or restates it. mattson-ellen and palm-anna-karin lean toward extension on the basis of reception and translation; sem-sandberg-steve and olsson-anders leave the question open. No member claims to have settled it volume by volume.

For Adonis: sward-anne describes the oeuvre as fully formed, so that maturity is a question of quality rather than development. carlberg-ingrid and sward-anne both state that the quality of the late work and the relative weight of poetry and essays are uncertain to them.

For Michon: whether a small corpus that is consistent from the 1980s onward demonstrates sustained quality (mattson-ellen) or is too narrow to establish significance across the whole oeuvre (olsson-anders, palm-anna-karin, sem-sandberg-steve).
palm-anna-karin raises, without developing, whether Alexis Wright's number of major novels is sufficient for the sustained-quality criterion.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: sem-sandberg-steve discloses a thematic overlap between his own work on Central Europe, Nazism and historical trauma and the subject matter of B008 (Claudio Magris), his second alternative. He reports no personal or institutional tie and does not propose recusal; the disclosure is recorded and not adjudicated.
carlberg-ingrid is a co-opted member whose actual committee voting status is undocumented. Her simulated vote is a modeling assumption, and the same assumption applies to any count that includes her.

olsson-anders, as chair, is also an explicit B012 supporter and so is counted among the four. His profile records scholarly interests in modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature and Celan, which are context only and not evidence of preference for any shortlisted writer.
No member reports a connection to a shortlisted writer. Members' own literary practice is stated as context, not as evidence of preference.
questions_for_round2: For the four B012 supporters: what specific textual or structural evidence from Solenoid, set against the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy, shows that the later work does something the earlier work did not, so that recurrence of motifs counts as development and not elaboration? Which colleagues can speak to the Romanian text, or to the translations, on this point?

For carlberg-ingrid and sward-anne: if the committee cannot test Arabic prosody and intertextual play through translation, what specific form of evidence (for example the quality of translations, the consistency of the poetry across decades, or critical reception in Arabic) would be sufficient to support a citation that names formal and linguistic renewal? Which claims should be left out of the wording?

For all members: should a B002 citation read 'poetic and critical oeuvre' or name the poetry alone, and should a B012 citation mention poetry at all? Please offer one concrete citation wording for each lead candidate that states only what the evidence supports.

For all members: is the translation risk roughly symmetrical between the poetry and prose claims, or does it bear harder on poetry? If asymmetrical, how should the committee weigh a claim it can verify only partly against one it can verify somewhat better?

For mattson-ellen and the other members who named Michon (B043): what evidence from the later work shows that the method extends beyond Small Lives and The Eleven, and would that change the weight given to breadth of significance?

For sem-sandberg-steve and any member who knows Magris's fiction: can a fuller case be made that the fiction, and not only the essay-narrative mixture, shows linguistic and imaginative invention comparable to the higher-ranked candidates?

For all members: if the committee finds that neither lead candidate can be stated precisely enough, is there any member who would prefer the no-award option P000 over B012 or B002 at this stage, and on what stated ground?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two explicit first preferences. Four members prefer B012 (Cărtărescu: mattson-ellen, olsson-anders, palm-anna-karin, sem-sandberg-steve) and two prefer B002 (Adonis: carlberg-ingrid, sward-anne). The chair is among the four B012 supporters, and the count includes carlberg-ingrid's simulated vote only as a modeling assumption. This summary does not treat the count as a ruling: the files show that members rate both writers highly and that the disagreement is mainly about which achievement can be stated and defended most precisely given translation limits, not about whether either writer is distinctive. Support is limited to what the six files say explicitly, and nomination frequency and opening rankings are not used as evidence. Round 2 should test the development-versus-elaboration question for Cărtărescu and the evidence available for the Adonis poetry, and should settle citation scope for both.
